[element-page-count]
=== `<page-count>` Page Count

Total number of pages in a work in print; by convention, each page or partial page is counted as one. Electronic-only works do not traditionally have page counts.

#### Usage/Remarks
This element is used both within the metadata describing a standards document and inside the deprecated NLM citation element.
##### Best Practice Metadata Usage

In the metadata for a standard, the <<element-page-count,`<page-count>`>> element can appear at two different levels: inside the <<element-counts,`<counts>`>> element and one level up, directly inside one of the metadata container elements (<<element-std-meta,`<std-meta>`>>,<<element-iso-meta,`<iso-meta>`>>, etc.) This double placement was necessary for ISO STS backwards compatibility. Best Practice going forward is to place the <<element-page-count,`<page-count>`>> element inside <<element-counts,`<counts>`>>.
##### Best Practice for Counting

Although a NISO STS standards-producing organization could choose to record _all_ the counts of objects in a standard using the <<element-count,`<count>`>> element, Best Practice is to use the specific count elements (<<element-fig-count,`<fig-count>`>>, <<element-equation-count,`<equation-count>`>>, <<element-word-count,`<word-count>`>>, etc.) whenever possible, using the <<element-count,`<count>`>> element only for ad hoc counts, organization-specific counts, standard-specific counts, and similar.

#### Related Elements

Inside the <<element-counts,`<counts>`>> container element are the counts of various components of the document: the generic count element <<element-count,`<count>`>> (for which the <<attribute-count-type,`@count-type`>> names what is being counted) and the specifically-named counting elements: <<element-fig-count,`<fig-count>`>> is the number of labeled figures (see definition of <<element-fig,`<fig>`>>). Do not include unlabeled graphics such as images embedded in table cells in the count of figures. Also do not make this the count of images referenced inside a figure, e.g., if a <<element-fig,`<fig>`>> has four panels (a-d) and each is a separate image file, the <<element-fig-count,`<fig-count>`>> is “`1`”, not “`4`”. <<element-table-count,`<table-count>`>> is the number of tables. Do not include arrays or uncaptioned/untitled tables in this count. <<element-equation-count,`<equation-count>`>> is the number of display equations (<<element-disp-formula,`<disp-formula>`>>). Do not include inline equations in the count (<<element-inline-formula,`<inline-formula>`>>). If you have a display equation that consists of multiple MathML objects, this counts as one equation; the <<element-equation-count,`<equation-count>`>> is “`1`”. <<element-ref-count,`<ref-count>`>> is either the number of references or (more properly) the number of citation elements _ within the bibliographic reference list_. Do not include cases of <<element-std,`<std>`>>, <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>>, or <<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>> elements that appear outside of <<element-ref-list,`<ref-list>`>>. <<element-page-count,`<page-count>`>> is the page count of the print or PDF item, including all Roman and Arabic number pages. <<element-word-count,`<word-count>`>> is the number of words in the document.
When a count needs to be divided into sub-counts, e.g., color vs. black-and-white figures, use the specific count element <<element-fig-count,`<fig-count>`>> for the total number of figures and then use separate <<element-count,`<count>`>> elements for the subsets, e.g.:
[source,xml]
....
<count count-type="fig-color" count="3"/>
<count count-type="fig-bw" count="7"/>
<fig-count count="10"/>
....

#### Attributes

* <<attribute-count,`@count`>> (REQUIRED)
#### Base Attributes

* <<attribute-id,`@id`>>
* <<attribute-xml-base,`@xml:base`>>

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-counts,`<counts>`>>, <<element-iso-meta,`<iso-meta>`>>, <<element-nat-meta,`<nat-meta>`>>, <<element-nlm-citation,`<nlm-citation>`>>, <<element-reg-meta,`<reg-meta>`>>, <<element-std-doc-meta,`<std-doc-meta>`>>, <<element-std-meta,`<std-meta>`>>
#### Description

This is an EMPTY element
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT  page-count   EMPTY                                        >
....

#### Tagged Samples

#### Page count inside `<std-meta>`

Number of pages in the standard
[source,xml]
....
...
<std-meta>
 ...
 <counts>
  <fig-count count="1"/>
  <table-count count="7"/>
  <equation-count count="141"/>
  <ref-count count="163"/>
  <page-count count="151"/>
 </counts>
</std-meta>
...
....
#### Page count inside `<iso-meta>`

Number of pages in the standard
[source,xml]
....
...
<iso-meta>
 ...
 <page-count count="48"/>
 <permissions>...</permissions>
</iso-meta>
...
....
